title: Earlier held-out years exceeded 2025 residual warm area in seven of eight ERSSTv5 models
abstract: We tested warm monthly sea area outside the equatorial Pacific in 2023-2025. We used ERSSTv5 and local calendar-month models fitted through 2022. Models had linear or quadratic trends, with or without three ENSO lag terms. Training began in 1960 or 1982. Warm months exceeded the training 90th percentile of model residuals. The primary quadratic model with ENSO terms gave mean warm area of 21.04% in 2023, 25.30% in 2024, and 19.72% in 2025. Across eight models, the 2025 fraction ranged from 15.45% to 23.58%. All eight models gave less warm area in 2025 than in 2024. Seven models had at least one earlier held-out year with greater mean warm area. The size and historical rank thus depended on the model and comparison rule. Each model was also compared with 23 earlier years held out from their fits. This descriptive test does not isolate an ENSO cause or give a return period. One product, trend extrapolation, sparse tail calibration and changing observation inputs limit the result.

The 2025 ocean report gives context for continued high SST. We read the indexed passage. This is not a new discovery of the global temperature record.
